question: Is buying Fairtrade-certified coffee an effective way to raise the incomes of the people who grow it?
answer: Certified cooperatives get a guaranteed minimum price when markets crash, plus a premium for community projects. A 2014 review by Dragusanu, Giovannucci and Nunn found certified farmers often received higher prices, better access to credit and steadier incomes. Where prices can halve within a couple of years, a floor matters more than an average.
move: Whichever side you took, who counts as the grower decides the answer.
counterpoint: Cooperatives often sell only part of their certified coffee on Fairtrade terms, and certification costs fall on farmers. A 2014 study in Ethiopia and Uganda led by Christopher Cramer found wage workers in Fairtrade-producing areas often earned less than comparable workers elsewhere. The poorest people in coffee are hired pickers, and the label pays the landholders.
reference: Dragusanu, Giovannucci & Nunn, The Economics of Fair Trade, Journal of Economic Perspectives, 2014
